//: Zeus tower - a 150-tile solid spire of HARDENED ROCK on an open plain (Stages 'hill'). The material is design, not decoration: hardened is ungrabbable and unplaceable at 10x stone HP, so the spire is terrain the player fights within rather than with - the climb cannot be short-cut by ripping a staircase out of the face or peeling the tower into throwable clods, which is what the block-throw kit does to any ordinary stone wall. The ground plane around it stays dirt-over-stone, so the plain is still normal workable terrain and the contrast is legible. The stage id and file names are kept as the encounter's proper noun so nothing downstream has to be renamed. Geometry: 37 tiles across where it meets the ground plane at world tile y 13, tapering three rows of rise per tile of run per side until it is 11 across, then easing off and dwindling the rest of the way to the single tile at y -137 the statue stands on. The dwindle is load-bearing: a constant-width pillar hides its own face from its own tip, so Zeus could not see a climber on the last hundred tiles of its own tower, and every Zeus laser gates on line of sight. The tip is bare - a one-tile summit cannot carry a rim wall, and would not want one: a parapet here would sit squarely between the statue and everything off to the side. It is solid all the way through - no interior, no stairs, no decks: the outside face is the route. AUTHORED BY GENERATOR: run scripts/gen-tower.py to rebuild every hill_*.txt from the geometry constants; do not hand-edit them. Rules cover only what a list of axis-aligned half-planes can say - the ground plane, the two outer walls that stop a knockback launch leaving the world, and open sky above the summit; a width that is a function of height is not expressible there, hence the generator. Extents 9 because the tower spans chunk rows -9..0. Statue, flock and shrike placement lives in Stage.cs.
